readerTitle: Thirty thousand readers and no income: who should pay?
caseNote: 가상 사례 (지역 맛집 뉴스레터, 엔지니어링 매니저 대상 뉴스레터) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 뉴스레터 수익화는 독자 수가 아니라 누가 무엇에 돈을 내는지로 정한다. 광고는 독자의 주의를 광고주에게 팔고, 구독은 글 자체를 독자에게 판다. 누가 돈을 내느냐에 따라 써야 할 글이 달라진다.
misconception: 독자가 많으면 광고든 유료화든 아무 모델이나 붙이면 돈이 된다. 광고 수익은 독자 수에만 달려 있다.

sources.text: BMO-02-02 구독, BMO-02-04 광고 개념 레슨의 내용을 적용
모든 수치와 인물은 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 3번 카드 계산: 스폰서 $500 × 주 4회 = 월 $2,000. 유료 구독 30,000명 × 3% = 900명 × $5 = 월 $4,500. 전환율 3%와 스폰서 단가 $500은 모두 설명용 가정이며, 카드 본문에도 추정치라고 적었습니다.
7번 카드에서 '일반 광고 네트워크는 대체로 노출량 기준으로 가격을 매긴다'는 일반론이 맞는지 확인하세요. 특정 단가나 수치는 일부러 넣지 않았습니다.
6번 카드의 '발행을 거르면 해지가 늘어난다'는 일반적인 경향으로만 적었습니다. 구체적인 해지율 수치는 넣지 않았습니다.

cards.title: Thirty thousand readers and no income: who should pay?
body: Maya writes a free weekly email about where to eat in her city: honest reviews, cheap lunches, new openings. After three years, 30,000 people read it.
It takes her 15 hours a week and earns her nothing. Then two emails arrive on the same morning. A restaurant group wants to sponsor her. A reader asks: *Can I just pay you?*

image.label: A writer at a café table reading two emails on a laptop
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 동네 카페 테이블에서 노트북을 보는 여성 작가. 화면에 이메일 두 통이 떠 있고, 하나는 포크와 나이프 아이콘(레스토랑 스폰서), 다른 하나는 하트와 동전 아이콘(독자). 실제 로고나 브랜드는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Which way to make money should Maya try first?
body: Maya only has time for one new project this year. Her readers come for one thing: reviews they can trust.
Which option should she start with?

options.feedback: **Advertising** earns money without charging readers. But here the sponsor is also a subject of her reviews, so every review starts to look paid for.

options.text: Start a paid tier for readers who want more
options.feedback: A **subscription** sells the newsletter itself to the people who value it most. It keeps Maya on her readers' side, and that is the reason they read her.

options.text: Sell ad space to local shops that aren't restaurants
options.feedback: This is **advertising** without the conflict, which helps. But the income depends on finding and keeping local sponsors, and that is a sales job she doesn't have time for yet.

cards.title: Same readers, different person paying.

breakdown.label: One sponsor
breakdown.detail: $500 an issue, four issues a month

breakdown.label: Paid tier
breakdown.detail: If 3% of readers pay $5 a month

cards.callout: These are guesses, not promises. What matters is what each number depends on. Ad income depends on how many people read. Subscription income depends on how much they care.

cards.title: Who pays decides what you write.
body: With **advertising**, readers use the newsletter and sponsors pay for it. Maya would be selling her readers' attention, so she would chase more readers and more opens.
With a **subscription**, readers are the customers. She would be selling the writing itself, so she would need pieces worth paying for every month.
Neither model is better in general. But each one pulls the newsletter in a different direction.

image.label: One newsletter with two arrows: readers' attention to sponsors, writing to paying readers
image.brief: 가운데 봉투 모양 뉴스레터. 왼쪽 화살표에는 "Attention → Sponsor", 오른쪽 화살표에는 "Writing → Reader" 라벨. 돈 흐름은 각각 반대 방향의 작은 동전 화살표로 표시. 로고는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: What goes behind the paywall?
body: Maya launches a paid tier at $5 a month. Now she has to decide what paying readers actually get.

options.text: The weekly reviews. Free readers get headlines only
options.feedback: This pushes readers to decide, but the free reviews are how new readers find her. Lock them away and the list stops growing, and so does the pool of future subscribers.

options.text: Free reviews stay. Paid readers get a monthly in-depth guide and a reader Q&A
options.feedback: The free issue keeps bringing people in, and the extras give fans a reason to pay. A **subscription** holds up when each month delivers something new.

options.text: Nothing changes. Paid readers simply support her
options.feedback: Loyal fans may pay out of goodwill, and it costs her no extra work. But with nothing new each month, it is harder to keep them paying.

cards.title: A subscription is a promise you keep every month.
body: Each month, paying readers quietly ask themselves whether it was worth it. Miss a few issues and cancellations follow.
Mixing models needs care too. Ads in the free issue can sit alongside a paid tier, but restaurant sponsors would bring the trust problem right back.
The math on card 3 is only a guess. Before building anything, Maya could ask readers to pay ahead for the first guide and see how many actually do.

cards.title: Now it's a newsletter for software teams.
body: Dev writes a weekly email for engineering managers. It has 6,000 readers, mostly team leads who choose the tools their teams use.
He wants to earn from it without hurting it. Which option fits best?

options.text: Sell one clearly labeled sponsor slot per issue to tool makers his readers might buy from
options.feedback: **Advertising** pays for the right attention, not just the most attention. To a tool company, 6,000 people who pick software can be worth a lot, and a clear label protects readers' trust.

options.text: Put every issue behind a $10 monthly paywall
options.feedback: A **subscription** could work, since some managers might expense it. But a paywall shrinks the list, and the readers that sponsors value most would mostly drift away.

options.text: Join a general ad network that fills ad slots automatically
options.feedback: It is easy to set up, but those ads are usually priced on volume, and 6,000 readers is small. Unrelated ads also waste what makes his readers valuable: who they are.

cards.title: Ask who pays, and what they are paying for.
body: A big audience is not yet a business. Advertising sells your readers' attention to someone else. A subscription sells your work to the readers themselves. Pick the model that keeps you on the side your audience trusts.
**Used today:** Subscriptions (whether to charge, and what goes behind the paywall) and Advertising (sponsor conflicts, and who the audience is versus how big it is).
**Try it today:** write down who your customers or followers are to an advertiser, and what they would pay you for directly. Which answer is stronger?

image.label: Two coins labeled Attention and Work on a balance scale
image.brief: 저울 양쪽에 동전 하나씩. 왼쪽 동전은 "Attention", 오른쪽 동전은 "Work" 라벨. 가운데 받침대에는 작은 봉투 아이콘. 단순하고 밝은 색감, 로고는 쓰지 않음.
